newsitem.title: MEXICO: Salinas to testify in Mexican murder probe - report.
newsitem.headline: Salinas to testify in Mexican murder probe - report.

text.p: Disgraced former President Carlos Salinas will be called to testify in the murder probe of a leading Mexican politician, newspapers said on Tuesday.

Officers from the Attorney General's office travelled to Dublin over the weekend to interview Salinas, who is living in self-imposed exile in Ireland, El Universal newspaper said. A spokesman for the Attorney General's office would not deny or confirm the reports.

Mexicans have long asked when the investigation into the 1994 assassination of Luis Donaldo Colosio, the presidential candidate of the ruling PRI party, would turn to Salinas, who left Mexico in disgrace last year when he was blamed for an economic crisis sparked by a disastrous peso devaluation soon after he left office.

Mexicans criticised Salinas' handling of the economy and charges have repeatedly emerged in Congress and the press of corruption in his administration. His brother Raul is in jail on charges of masterminding another political assassination and is under investigation for stashing millions of dollars in foreign bank accounts.
The former president left Mexico days after his brother's arrest in February, 1995. His lawyer Juan Velazquez did not confirm or deny that the probe was now focusing on his client.

"Don Carlos is interested in testifying about anything he is alleged to have done," Velazquez told Radio Red. He denied press reports that he flew to New York or Dublin over the weekend to meet Salinas.
